newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: OLYMPCS-WOMEN URGE IOC TO STOP GENDER TESTING.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPCS-WOMEN URGE IOC TO STOP GENDER TESTING.

text.p: The world conference on Women and Sport urged the International Olympic Committee (IOC) on Wednesday to stop the present method of gender testing at the Olympic Games.
The issue of gender testing was the most contentious of 16 recommendations to be presented to the IOC.
Many of the 200 delegates from 96 nations attending the three-day conference objected to tests on women only and complained that present testing procedures were inaccurate.
"The issue is people think that it's a bad idea to treat people one way and not treat men the same way," said Anita Defrantz, chairwoman of the conference and a U.S IOC member.
"Why should you have to test women to find out they're women and not test men?"
The conference will also urge the IOC to continue their efforts to get an equal number of events for women and men on the Olympic program.
"We're getting close to parity on this issue and perhaps will be there by Sydney," said Defrantz.
